hypothesis: Baseline. No hypothesis -- this is the number later changes are measured against.
result: 35/36 correct. The single failure is g06 attempt 1: the agent grouped the mix-vs-rate decomposition by a dimension where rate dominates, concluded 'rate', and passed verification -- every number was cited, the arithmetic reconciled, the conclusion was wrong. pass^1 was 1.0 on an earlier run; pass^3 is 0.917, which is the gap averaging hides.
notes: Seeded-anomaly detection scored 1/3 strict (3/3 months flagged, 1 cause correctly named) against a target of 2/3. The agent does not drill into dimensions unless asked, so a regional and a category-level anomaly were invisible. That is the next experiment, not a fix to fold in silently.

hypothesis: numbers_backed failures on 'why' questions are a grammar gap, not model error: the model cites segments[0].delta and the verifier reads the indices as typed digits.
evidence: runs/20261006-181939: FAIL numbers_backed '6 numbers typed: 17, 0, 17, 0, 17, 1' -- all six were indices inside {{e17.segments[0].delta}}. Repair ran and recorded not_landed, correctly: no reprompt can satisfy a grammar that cannot express the citation.
result: Same question after the fix: numbers_backed PASS, 11 placeholders resolved, 5 steps instead of 13. The repair cycle was being spent fighting the verifier.
notes: Fourth verifier/grader defect this session. All four were the measurement being wrong, not the agent. Note this fix lives in report/ and verifier/, both outside triage's PATCHABLE list -- an autonomous fixer must not be able to 'fix' a false positive by loosening the check that raised it.

hypothesis: Spider tasks fail because sql mode exposes the prose-mode arithmetic tools. Their schemas are all described in terms of evidence ids, and 7 of 15 answers wrote {{e4.zero_value}} INTO their SQL -- without ever calling one of those tools. Restricting the tool surface should remove the idiom and raise the number of scorable answers.
variable_changed: sql mode's tool list: 7 tools -> 4 (search_catalog, describe_table, get_join_path, run_sql). Prompt also gained one line about double braces.
result: End-to-end accuracy 33.3% -> 66.7%. Every answer became scorable (9 -> 15) and placeholder leakage went 7 -> 0, which is the mechanism the hypothesis named. Tokens fell 8% as a side effect of a smaller tool surface.
caveats: k=1 on 15 of 135 tasks. The placeholder mechanism is strongly evidenced (7 -> 0 is not noise), but 5 -> 10 correct on n=15 at k=1 is not a precise effect size. Needs k>=3 and the full 135 before quoting 66.7% as the agent's accuracy.
notes: Scored with Spider's own evaluate.py in exec_result mode. Two benchmarks exist in this repo and should not be conflated: Spider 2.0-Lite (135 local tasks, evals/runner.py) and Spider2-DBT (64 tasks, evals/dbt/runner.py). This experiment is Lite only.

hypothesis: Spider2-DBT failures are specification-discovery: the agent does not know what models/*.yml declares. Telling it to read every .yml first, verify each declared model exists, and check COUNT(*) against COUNT(DISTINCT grain_key) should raise pass@1.
variable_changed: evals/dbt/prompts/main.md gained a 'Read the schema files first' section
task_set: Spider2-DBT, 64 tasks (68 minus 4 with no gold DB), k=3
result: REFUTED, and expensively. Accuracy moved 0.2344 -> 0.224, inside overlapping noise bands (0.219-0.250 vs 0.188-0.250) and therefore not a real change. The non-noise signal was cost: max_turns 5 -> 29, budget failures 4 -> 23, mean input tokens 280k -> 479k, cost $5.79 -> $9.76. The longer prompt bought diligence at a bad exchange rate -- the agent spent its budget inspecting instead of building.
note: The .yml files were not the missing information. That pointed at discovery as the real gap, which exp3 tested directly.

hypothesis: The agent cannot discover what dbt built. The gateway refused information_schema (169 of 361 rejections) and the sandbox has no describe tool, so the agent guessed schema qualification and was wrong 142 times. Opening the catalog should remove both categories.
variable_changed: gateway: engine catalog exempt from the allowlist (information_schema / sqlite_master); refusals name the schema-qualified reference; DuckDB describe() covers every user schema. Prompt reverted to baseline.
result: CONFIRMED on mechanism, NULL on accuracy -- which is what was predicted in writing before the run. The two target categories collapsed: catalog refusals 168 -> 0 across 7,312 calls, schema qualification 95 -> 11 (-88%), overall failed-call rate 6.5% -> 4.0%. Accuracy moved 0.2344 -> 0.250 (15 -> 16 of 64) with fully overlapping noise bands, and pass^3 is identical at 0.156. Task-level churn confirms it is noise: 5 tasks gained, 4 lost, 16 shared.
note: Opening one door surfaced the next: non-SELECT refusals rose 33 -> 77, all metadata (59 DESCRIBE, 18 SHOW). Knowing introspection works, the agent reached for the more natural forms and the SELECT-only rule refused them. Same bug, one layer out. The remaining failures are unchanged in character: edit_file text-not-found 95, read no-such-file 65 -- turn waste, not capability -- and the scored failures are still aggregation logic (row_count, values), which no discovery fix can reach.

hypothesis: Exp2 (telling the agent to read models/*.yml) failed on delivery cost, not on being wrong. Splicing the same content in from the host at zero turn cost should test the hypothesis properly, and should most plausibly help the 7 'missing table' failures where a required model was never built.
variable_changed: evals/dbt/spec.py: models/**/*.yml condensed (names, descriptions, column names) and appended to the task instruction by the runner. ~800 tokens, median 2.6 KB.
task_set: Spider2-DBT, 64 tasks, k=3 (crashed during attempt 3; 2 complete attempts compared against the same 2 attempts of the control)
result: REFUTED. The block costs ~800 tokens to deliver and raised mean input tokens by 147,000 per attempt -- 180x its own size -- because it made the agent do more work, not because it is long. Mean turns 19.3 -> 23.6, attempts hitting the 40-turn cap 2 -> 19, cost +51%, and 28 passes against 31. Naming a mean of 11.1 models and saying each must exist sent the agent off building models the task never asked for. This is exp2's failure mode reproduced through a cheaper delivery mechanism, which means the mechanism was never the problem.
decision: revert (inject_model_spec = false; code and tests kept, flag-controlled)
note: Measured before the run that only 2% of 766 declared models state their grain explicitly and 74% say nothing about it, so the premise was already weak and that was recorded beforehand. The run itself died on ENOSPC at attempt 3 of 3 after ~3h and $7 -- a 466 GB disk filled by ~28 MB x 192 attempts of workspace and submission copies. Fixed by pruning each attempt once scored and refusing a run below 8 GB free.

hypothesis: The agent stops when `dbt run` exits 0, which only means the SQL compiled (141 of 147 baseline failures had a clean exit). 80% of these projects declare column tests -- 809 not_null, 280 unique -- targeting exactly the measured failure modes, and the agent ran `test` in 23% of attempts. Running those assertions and handing failures back for one repair pass should convert flaky tasks.
variable_changed: runner.test_gate(): after the agent stops, run `dbt test`; on failure hand the failing assertions back for one repair pass. Structural gate, not a prompt line.
result: NULL, and it costs. pass@1 0.250 -> 0.234, inside overlapping noise (0.219-0.266 vs 0.203-0.266) and pass^3 identical at 0.156, for +16% cost and +19% turns. The gate works mechanically: it fired on every completed attempt and named the right rows -- provider001's assertions flagged the same 2,857 rows an independent gold diff found. It simply does not convert. Over 157 gated attempts, those whose assertions passed clean scored 0.259 and those that failed and were repaired scored 0.222; retail001 passed, was repaired, then failed.
decision: revert (test_gate = false; code and tests kept)
note: Decisive because it isolates awareness from capability. The agent was handed the exact failing rows, by name, and could not use them. Together with the catalog fix (168 refused reads -> 0, accuracy unchanged) and two spec-injection failures, five interventions have now targeted what the agent KNOWS and none has moved pass@1 out of 0.219-0.266. The remaining gap is authoring the SQL.

hypothesis: Five interventions targeting what the agent KNOWS moved nothing, so the gap is authoring the SQL. reasoning_effort was plumbed through but never set, so Luna ran at the API default. Raising it to high should target capability directly, and costs ~$1 because reasoning bills as output.
variable_changed: roles.main.reasoning_effort = "high" (was unset/default). test_gate off in the same commit so this is one variable against the control.
result: NULL on pass@1, and it widens variance. 0.250 -> 0.255 is +0.3 tasks. The change was real at the input (reasoning tokens 1,700 -> 3,745, 2.2x) but the output did not follow. Attempts 1 and 2 landed at 0.297 and 0.281, both above the control's entire range, and attempt 3 came in at 0.188, below it -- the noise band WIDENED from 0.219-0.266 to 0.188-0.297. Attempt 3 is not explained by budget or effort: 23.0 turns and 3,726 reasoning tokens against 22.7/3,778 and 22.9/3,733 for its siblings. Same inputs, worse draw. Pass rate among completed attempts is 0.246 against the control's 0.237. Cost +57%, turn-cap hits 6 -> 17.
note: I called this a success after two attempts and was wrong; the third erased it. A per-attempt rate is one sample and this benchmark swings +-2 tasks. Only pass^3 moved, 0.156 -> 0.172 (10 -> 11 tasks passing all three), which is the one weak positive. Also measured: capped attempts passed at 6/17 against 0.246 for completed ones, which argues AGAINST raising max_turns -- hitting the cap is not what loses these tasks.

hypothesis: f1001's finishes_by_driver sits in the starting database matching gold exactly (860 rows, zeros, no NULLs); the agent rewrote it and introduced the 75 NULLs that fail it. f1001/f1002/f1003 each rewrote ALL their scored models and each touched 15-18 .sql files for a task needing 3-4. Telling the agent to leave working models alone should recover those tasks.
variable_changed: evals/dbt/prompts/main.md +4 sentences (330 chars): most of this project already works, change only what the task asks for, check whether a model already builds before rewriting it.
result: BEST RESULT SO FAR, BUT THE STATED MECHANISM IS REFUTED. pass@1 0.250 -> 0.276 (+1.7 tasks), pass^3 0.156 -> 0.188 (10 -> 12 tasks passing all three, the largest consistency gain measured), and it is CHEAPER: $5.45 vs $5.76, 18.2 turns vs 19.4. Every attempt landed at or above the control's pass@1. BUT the three tasks it targeted did not move: f1001, f1002 and f1003 are still 0/3 each, and the F1 tasks still touched 52 .sql files against 54 in the control -- the agent essentially ignored the instruction where it was aimed. Task-level churn is 9 gained / 7 lost, the signature of the flaky set. The instruction did change behaviour diffusely: .sql files touched per attempt 3.82 -> 3.18 (-17%). Execution failures tripled, 3 -> 10.
note: The noise bands overlap (0.219-0.266 vs 0.250-0.297), so +1.7 tasks is suggestive, not established. This project's own guidance says detecting a 2-task change needs k=6, and one earlier experiment was called a success after two attempts and reversed on the third. Replicating with the identical config to pool into k=6 is the next step, not another new variable.

hypothesis: Replicate exp7 with the identical config to pool into k=6, because its noise band overlapped the control's and this project has already been fooled once by a two-attempt result.
task_set: Spider2-DBT, 64 tasks, k=3 (pooled with exp7 for k=6)
result: DID NOT REPLICATE. The second run landed at 0.250, exactly the control. Pooled k=6: 0.281, 0.250, 0.297, 0.266, 0.250, 0.234 -> mean 0.263 = 16.8/64, sd 0.023, 95% CI 0.245-0.281 (15.7-18.0 tasks). The control's 0.250 sits INSIDE that interval. The true effect is +0.8 tasks and is not established. exp7's 17.7/64 was a favourable draw, which is the second time in this project a single k=3 run overstated an effect that the next run erased.
decision: keep on cost, not on accuracy
note: The secondary effects ARE consistent across both runs and worth keeping: turns 19.4 -> 18.2 and 17.6, cost $5.76 -> $5.45 and $5.23, .sql files touched 3.82 -> 3.18. The agent is cheaper and faster with accuracy indistinguishable. Execution failures rose 3 -> 10 in run 1, worth watching. The stated mechanism remains refuted: f1001/f1002/f1003 are 0/3 in both runs.

hypothesis: The no-rewrite prompt doubled execution failures (3 -> 10 and 7, all dbt exit 1) by making the agent conservative enough to leave models broken. zuora001 and shopify_holistic_reporting001 were new, the latter a 56%-flaky task now failing to build. Adding 'leaving a model alone is not the same as leaving it broken; the project must still build' should recover those attempts.
variable_changed: evals/dbt/prompts/main.md +3 sentences. Also, independently: scoring._repair_gold_filename resolves the eval set's gold-filename typo for xero_new001/xero_new002/social_media001 inside the staged copy (recovers no passes; makes them fail for the real reason).
result: THE MECHANISM WORKED AND BOUGHT NOTHING. Execution failures fell 10 and 7 -> 3, back to the control's level, and the only remaining one is sap001, which has genuinely missing source data. zuora001 and shopify_holistic_reporting001 no longer fail to build. But pass@1 did not move: 0.245 against 0.250 for the control. zuora001 is 0/3 in every configuration ever run -- fixing its build did not help because it fails on content. shopify_holistic_reporting001 went 2/3, 1/3, 2/3, 1/3 across four configurations: pure flakiness, no trend.
note: Pooled over all 9 attempts of the no-rewrite family (182055, 220241, 034737): 0.2569 = 16.4/64, 95% CI 15.6-17.3. The control's 16.0 is inside it. This is the tightest estimate in the project and the gap to 20 is 3.6 tasks. Another confirmation of the diagnosis: 7 attempts' worth of build failures were repaired and the pass rate did not move, because those tasks fail on content whether or not they build.

hypothesis: exp6 reverted reasoning_effort='high' on a k=3 null whose 95% CI was 12.0-20.6 tasks -- uselessly wide -- and cited a '+57% cost' that was really 70c under the corrected pricing. Its two best attempts were two of the four best ever recorded. Re-test at k=6 against the current prompt family.
variable_changed: roles.main.reasoning_effort = 'high'. Everything else is the current kept configuration (catalog access, no-rewrite + must-build prompt). One variable.
result: NOT ESTABLISHED, but the retest was right and the original revert was not. Point estimate 16.4 -> 17.3 tasks (+0.9). Difference 95% CI -0.7 to +2.5 tasks, t=1.11: zero is inside it. What k=6 did buy is a usable interval -- exp6's k=3 CI was 12.0-20.6, which could not have distinguished anything. Two further observations: there was no collapse attempt (minimum 15 tasks against exp6's 12), so the 'widens variance' conclusion from exp6 does not survive a larger sample; and one attempt scored 20/64, the target, the only time it has been reached. Turn-cap hits rose 6 -> 30 and cost nothing: capped attempts passed at 0.267 against 0.271 for completed ones, so raising max_turns stays unindicated.
decision: keep (higher point estimate, no variance penalty, $3.86 for k=6)
note: The honest summary of exp6 vs exp9 is that the first was decided on evidence too weak to decide anything, under a cost model inflated 4.5x. The answer is still not significant at k=6; establishing +0.9 tasks would need roughly k=24 against k=36, about $25 and 30 hours. That is now affordable, which it was not believed to be.
